title: Redwood Security BCDR / Incident Response & SLA Review - Evergreen Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed Evergreen Health's incident response and BCDR expectations. Discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO options, audit logging retention, KMS and encryption at rest/in transit, RTO/RPO targets, SLA uptime, and the escalation/on-call process. Action items agreed: share SOC 2 evidence, runbook examples, and a proposed SLA amendment for Dedicated customers; schedule a follow-up bench test for failover and RTO verification.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary (Maya)
Send internal escalation matrix and on-call runbook sample (Jamal)
Schedule 1-hour failover bench test with Evergreen SREs w/in 3 weeks (Priya)
Provide drafted SLA clause for RTO/RPO and uptime commitments (Maya)
Customer to share current internal RTO/RPO requirements and compliance checklist (Lina)
Agree on list of log types and retention period for audit logs (Sara)
action_items: Maya Chen - Share SOC2 Type II and ISO summary - 2025-12-05
Jamal Ortiz - Export sample audit log schema and retention options - 2025-12-10
Priya Nair - Schedule failover bench test (coordinate with Diego) - 2025-12-18
Lina Patel - Send Evergreen RTO/RPO requirements doc - 2025-12-08
Diego Morales - Prepare dev/stage endpoints for test - 2025-12-15
transcript: 00:00 Maya: ok hi everyone thanks for joining we wanted to make sure we covered Evergreen's incident response and B C D R expectations today
00:08 Lina: thanks Maya yep we appreciate this, we had some follow ups from the security review and want to confirm RTO and escalation behavior

00:15 Jamal: hi all jamal here i am the se for redwood i can walk through runbooks, on-call, and the SLA specifics — quick agenda: SOC2/ISO posture, auth/RBAC, logging, encryption, then incident response and RTO/RPO and escalation run through
00:30 Tom: quick note, our compliance gap is audit log retention and proof of key management — we use an external KMS already so want to see how Redwood integrates

00:42 Maya: good call. we have SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for RBAC, and for KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). we also have on-prem HSM options for private deployments
01:05 Sara: can you confirm what is in the audit logs — like request headers, full payloads, redacted PII? retention windows?

01:15 Jamal: yeah so by default we log request metadata, model and route, token counts, latencies, and error traces. payload logging is off by default for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private you can enable request-level logs with redaction rules. retention tiers: 30 days default, 90/365 as paid retention add-ons
01:40 Lina: our policy requires 1 year for security-relevant logs; is that doable?
01:46 Jamal: yes we can do 365 retention as part of an add-on; we'll share the exact cost matrix. we'll also show the export paths to your SIEM via secure S3 or direct streaming
02:02 Tom: what about encryption in transit and at rest? do you hold plaintext anywhere, and how are keys rotated?

02:12 Maya: in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3 end to end. at rest we encrypt with per-customer keys when you bring your own KMS; keys never leave the customer's KMS. for hosted customers without BYOK we manage keys but customers can opt into Redwood-managed KMS with standard rotation policies. key rotation for BYOK is customer controlled via KMS, and we support key versioning and re-encryption flows
02:40 Sara: SOC2 and ISO — can you share reports and scoping? we need evidence for our vendor assessment
02:48 Maya: yes we can provide SOC 2 Type II report for the control period and an ISO 27001 summary. we'll strip any customer-specific data. i'll put that in the follow-up packet
03:00 Diego: on BCDR — what's your documented RTO and RPO for hosted vs dedicated vs private?

03:10 Jamal: good question. for hosted API we have multi-region routing with fallbacks; RTO for control plane incidents is usually 30-60 minutes for degraded failover and RPO is near-zero for stateless requests but depends on caching for long conversations. for Dedicated customers we provide SLA-backed uptime targets and can negotiate RTO/RPO. for private on-prem deployments RTO/RPO are customer-specific and documented in the deployment runbook
03:40 Tom: can you quantify that — example numbers?

03:45 Jamal: Sure. Typical SLA tiers: 99.9% monthly uptime for standard Dedicated, 99.95% for premium. For RTO we aim for <60 minutes for control plane failover in Dedicated, and <15 minutes for data-plane routing fallback in multi-region deployments. RPO targets: near-zero for requests (we don't rely on long-lived writes), but for session state you can choose KV cache persistence options; RPO can be set to 0-15s depending on configuration. these are draft numbers — we'll put a proposed clause in writing
04:10 Lina: we need contractual RTO of <30 minutes for our critical endpoints and RPO <60s. is that realistic?
04:18 Maya: for Dedicated/premium we can support a contractual RTO <30m with capacity commitments and runbook tests; we'll need to add that to the SLA and agree on test acceptance criteria
04:30 Sara: what does the escalation chain look like — pager, SE, engineering — and do you provide 24/7 on-call for incidents?

04:38 Jamal: Redwood provides tiered escalation: first response by support engineers (business hours standard), for Dedicated we provide 24/7 on-call with an on-call rotation and a named escalation engineer. we also provide a customer-specific escalation matrix and a post-incident report template
04:55 Maya: and the on-call contact/leads can be pushed in the contract; we keep an incident commander model and will include runbooks for failover, rollback, and communication templates
05:10 Diego: are there runbook examples you can share? we want to validate procedures and measure RTO in a bench test

05:18 Jamal: yes we'll share sanitized runbook examples and a mechanics doc on how failover is executed. we'll also run a bench test with Evergreen SREs: simulate region outage, failover to secondary region, measure RTO and any data exposure
05:35 Tom: how do you handle KV cache and conversation continuity during failover — we can't lose ongoing sessions

05:42 Jamal: we have prefix and KV cache replication strategies. for low-latency session replication we recommend Dedicated with cross-region cache replication. for hosted standard, session continuity is best-effort across region failovers and can incur session replay or truncated context. we'll show expected behavior in the test
06:05 Lina: data residency — some of our data must remain in-region (EU). if we go hosted do you support EU-only regions and contractual residency?

06:15 Maya: yes, we have region pinning and can limit processing to EU regions. for private deployments you can host entirely in your VPC or on-prem. we also support contractual clauses for data residency
06:30 Sara: auditability — will you supply immutable audit logs and attestations for incident timelines?
06:36 Jamal: yes immutable logs are available as append-only exports with tamper-evidence hashes for Dedicated customers; we can also provide signed timeline attestations on request
06:50 Tom: what about legal/forensics — if there's a security event we need chain-of-custody and support for investigations

06:58 Maya: we provide forensic artifacts and cooperate under our data processing agreement; we have an escalation playbook with forensic steps and a dedicated security contact for high-severity incidents
07:10 Sara: ok on the encryption front do you ever decrypt customer payloads for debugging? what's the process?

07:20 Jamal: we do not decrypt customer data without explicit permission; for Redwood-managed keys we have internal procedures and audit logs for any access. for BYOK we cannot decrypt without you providing key material or an explicit key unlock procedure. debugging with request payloads requires a ticket and explicit customer authorization
07:40 Lina: would you support SAML + SCIM provisioning and role-based access controls that mirror our internal roles?
07:47 Maya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported; RBAC can map to your groups and we can enforce least privilege per route and per model. we'll share the mapping guide
08:00 Tom: SLAs and credit mechanisms — what happens if you miss RTO/RPO or uptime guarantees?

08:07 Jamal: we typically offer service credits for downtime in the SLA; for critical failures where RTO commitments aren't met we'll accept escalated remedies defined in the SLA, including higher credits or termination rights for repeated breaches. details will be in the contract
08:25 Maya: one ask from our legal team is to see the post-incident reports template — we will share the PIR template and a sample redacted PIR
08:34 Sara: about monitoring and observability — do you expose traces and token-level latency breakdowns? that's important for our SLOs

08:42 Jamal: yes we expose per-route dashboards, token-level latency, and cost breakdowns. we also provide tracing hooks to plug into your APM and alerting alerts based on error rates and latency thresholds
09:00 Diego: for the bench test are you asking to do both simulated region failover and a control-plane incident?
09:06 Priya: ideally both, yes — we can coordinate two separate tests or a combined scenario. we'll propose dates in the follow-up
09:15 Lina: what about contact points during a live incident — do we get a link to a war room or slack channel?
09:22 Maya: for Dedicated we provision a customer war-room Slack channel and shared incident doc during high-severity events and provide an on-call engineer and incident commander contact
09:35 Sara: audit log searchability — can you support exporting logs to our SIEM with field-level redaction?
09:42 Jamal: yes secure streaming to your SIEM is supported; we can apply field-level redaction prior to export or provide tokenized fields
10:00 Tom: okay let's talk about timelines for contractual updates — we expect SOC2 evidence this week and a proposed SLA within 7 business days
10:08 Maya: we will deliver SOC2 and ISO summary by Friday, and draft SLA clause in 7 business days. jamal will drop the runbook and log schema in the next week
10:20 Lina: great, once we get that we'll schedule the bench test. we want to run by end of year if possible
10:28 Priya: we'll aim to coordinate with Diego and send calendar invites after the docs are shared
10:35 Diego: one more technical question — do you support customer-managed network egress controls for private deployments?
10:42 Jamal: yes for private and VPC deployments we support customer-managed egress, private links, and peering, plus strict network policies. public hosted endpoints are behind our managed gateway
10:58 Sara: any notable limitations or gotchas we should plan for in the test?

11:05 Jamal: biggest gotchas are session continuity on hosted tier and potential cold-start latencies during scale events; for mission-critical endpoints we recommend Dedicated with pre-warmed capacity and cross-region replication
11:25 Tom: ok thanks everyone this was helpful. can we do a short recap of next steps?

11:32 Maya: recap: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO, runbook examples, audit log schema, draft SLA clause; Evergreen to share RTO/RPO requirements and prep test endpoints. schedule bench test — target by 2025-12-18. action owners listed in follow-up
11:55 Lina: yes that works thanks
12:00 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and put materials in the shared drive
12:05 End of recording
